discovery: Photonic crystals: the photonic band gap concept and its realization for controlling light emission and confinement
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures can open a photonic band gap, forbidding propagation of light in a frequency range. Yablonovitch showed that this suppresses spontaneous emission; John showed that it leads to strong localization of light and new forms of light–matter interaction. Yablonovitch then built the first three-dimensional band-gap structure. Noda turned the concept into working physics and devices: complete three-dimensional band gaps at optical wavelengths, ultrahigh-Q nanocavities that store light in volumes near the diffraction limit, and photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers that now give watt-class, single-mode, beam-steerable output. Photonic crystals changed how we treat the electromagnetic vacuum: it became something one can engineer. That shift underlies slow light, cavity quantum electrodynamics with quantum dots, single-photon sources, nanolasers, topological photonics and energy-efficient on-chip optical interconnects. It is a fundamental conceptual discovery with deep experimental confirmation and broad technological impact.
